First release.

- Tables over Bluetooth LE and Wi-Fi together — no internet, no host, no account
- Solo play against bots, each bot a whole device on a local mesh

releases.app_summary: Board games around a real table — phones play together over Bluetooth, no internet, no host, no account.
releases.app_content:
Table Mesh lets a group of friends play a board game together at a real table,
each on their own phone. The phones find each other over Bluetooth (and Wi-Fi
when there is one) and form a small mesh: no internet, no server, no account,
and no phone is the host. Every phone runs the game's rules itself and only the
moves travel, so a game keeps going when a phone sleeps, drops out or restarts —
it catches up from the others when it comes back. A tablet in the middle can
show the whole board.

**Included: Mensch ärgere Dich nicht** — the German family classic for 2–4
players, with the full rules, table dice or your own real dice, a referee
override, bots to play against on your own, and a table view for the tablet.

**More games from Nostr.** Games are small sandboxed modules. *Find games*
searches Nostr for game releases (kind 7529) and downloads them from Blossom
servers, checking every byte against the game's hash before it is installed.
A game module has no network access and no storage: it can only receive moves
and propose moves.

**When something goes wrong, you see it.** Every phone keeps the whole game
history, hash-chained. If two phones ever disagree, the table turns red and a
person decides which history to keep — nothing is merged behind your back.

This is an early release. The Bluetooth mesh has been tested extensively in
simulation and on emulators; reports from real tables with several phones are
very welcome.

releases.app_summary: A Nostr-powered personal cloud and self-hosted AI — notes, calendar, contacts, files, passwords
releases.app_content:
PosterChan is the Android half of a **Nostr-powered personal cloud** and a **self-hosted AI powerhouse**
that runs on hardware you own. Your notes, calendar, contacts, files, passwords and mail live as encrypted
Nostr events on a relay you run — no account with anybody, no subscription, no vendor holding the keys.

**The personal cloud**

- **Notes**: private, offline-first, encrypted to your own key. Write with no signal; it syncs when you have one.
- **Calendar and contacts**: real **CalDAV/CardDAV**, so your phone's own calendar and contacts apps sync
  with your node like any other server — one account for both.
- **Files and folder sync**: keep Documents and Pictures in step between phone and desktop through your own
  node. Contents are encrypted before they leave the device, so your server stores a folder it cannot read.
- **Password manager**: logins, one-time codes (TOTP) and a generator, with **Android autofill** offering
  them in your other apps and browsers. Every entry is encrypted on your device — the relay holds ciphertext.
- **Bookmark sync**: the companion add-on (Firefox, Chrome, Edge, Brave) keeps bookmarks in step across
  browsers, sealed with the same vault key.
- **Mail**: your own IMAP/SMTP accounts, mirrored as encrypted events so search works without a round trip.

**The AI powerhouse**

- **Chat**: streaming LLM conversations against your own models or any OpenAI-compatible API.
- **Generation**: images, music and video, produced on your own GPU rather than someone's rented one.
- **Private search**: a metasearch engine bundled with your node, with AI overviews and citations.
- **Live streaming**: go live from your camera or screen (NIP-53), and watch other people's streams.
- **Voice and video calls**: 1:1 and group, over WebRTC.

**And a full Nostr client**: feeds, threads, profiles, DMs, communities, mini apps and a web-of-trust relay.

Self-hostable by design — point the app at your own instance; the default is poster.place.
